assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational account of how collateral constraints amplify credit cycles and connect financial conditions to aggregate fluctuations.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore provide the central collateral-cycle mechanism; Gertler is a major contributor to the financial-accelerator formulation.
assessment.maturity: The framework has shaped macro-finance theory, empirical work, and policy analysis for decades.
uncertainties: The precise division between the collateral-cycle and financial-accelerator strands complicates a compact attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their analysis of credit risk, search frictions, and over-the-counter markets transformed understanding of important real financial-market institutions.
assessment.attribution: Duffie, Pedersen, and Garleanu have closely associated and complementary contributions to the theoretical architecture of OTC markets.
assessment.maturity: The work is well established, highly consequential, and especially salient after the financial crisis.
uncertainties: The candidate bundle spans several linked finance contributions rather than one sharply bounded discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on liquidity, funding constraints, and asset prices has made a durable contribution to modern finance and systemic-risk analysis.
assessment.attribution: Amihud supplied seminal liquidity measurement, while Pedersen and Brunnermeier developed influential theoretical and systemic implications.
assessment.maturity: The concepts are deeply embedded in asset-pricing research and practical financial-risk analysis.
uncertainties: The broad literature contains several plausible additional contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work brought household leverage and mortgage-credit dynamics to the center of explanations of financial crises and macroeconomic downturns.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the clearest joint architects of the empirical household-debt agenda; Campbell provides important related foundations.
assessment.maturity: Its implications have been extensively studied since the global financial crisis and remain policy relevant.
uncertainties: The breadth of the household-finance and macro-finance literature makes the three-person attribution contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law-and-finance research redirected attention to investor protection and legal institutions as determinants of financial development and corporate governance.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Shleifer, and Vishny were central to the core legal-origins program and its influential empirical evidence.
assessment.maturity: The work has had long-standing influence across finance, development, and comparative institutional analysis.
uncertainties: Causal interpretation and the legal-origins thesis have faced substantial scholarly debate.
Florencio Lopez-de-Silanes is also an important contributor to the program.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection supplied a powerful and empirically productive revision of trade theory and welfare analysis.
assessment.attribution: Melitz developed the signature heterogeneous-firm framework, with Helpman and Redding making major connected contributions.
assessment.maturity: The approach is central to contemporary international-trade research and has accumulated extensive empirical support.
uncertainties: There are difficult boundary questions about which contributors belong in a limited prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design created a general language for strategic information provision with wide applications.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica is central to the seminal persuasion formulation; Bergemann and Morris made core contributions to information design and its foundations.
assessment.maturity: The field has rapidly become influential across theory, industrial organization, and policy design.
uncertainties: Its comparatively recent expansion leaves less time to assess its ultimate durability.
Matthew Gentzkow is also closely associated with the foundational persuasion contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework provided a tractable and influential way to quantify how distortions across firms affect productivity and income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow are particularly central to the empirical quantitative framework, with Restuccia a major contributor to the broader program.
assessment.maturity: The framework has generated a large literature on firm-level distortions, productivity, and development.
uncertainties: Measurement of distortions and interpretation of wedges remain contested.
The empirical magnitude of misallocation effects varies across settings.
